title: A Harvest for the Well
premise: Mirabel Montrose, a surveyor who learned invisibility from a childhood spent in her grandmother's haunted house, is hired to appraise the old Well House before its sale. She discovers every photograph taken there now contains an extra chair—and whoever sits in it is slowly learning her name. The house was never haunted; it was fed, for generations, by the Montrose family's covenant of silence, and the sale will leave it starving and loose upon the town. To survive until sunrise and end the covenant, Mirabel must stop hiding, claim her inheritance, and offer the house not another soul but her own grief—unmaking the bargain her ancestors made, at the cost of the found family she built inside its walls.
about_author: U. M. Oyelaran is a Nigerian-British writer of quiet horror whose stories explore what families owe to the places that raised them. A former land surveyor, Oyelaran brings an appraiser's precision to the geography of dread.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Mirabel arrives at Well House to appraise it for sale, keeping her professional distance and her lights on. She notices the house measures larger inside than out, and a chair sits in the parlor that isn't on her survey. POV: Mirabel. Beat: wary competence masking old fear—the reader feels she's been here before.

chapters.title: An Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Mirabel develops the property photographs and finds an additional chair in every frame, sometimes occupied by a shape her eye refuses to focus on. She calls her grandmother, who hangs up after saying only, 'Count the doors.' POV: Mirabel. Beat: dread crystallizes from unease into evidence.

chapters.title: Doors, Counted
chapters.summary: Mirabel returns at dusk to verify: the house has one more door than her measurements allow, and it is warm. She meets Theo, the young caretaker who has lived in the gatehouse alone, and the two form a wary alliance over shared coffee and shared denial. POV: Mirabel. Beat: first flicker of found family—she is not alone in this.

chapters.title: What Grandma Kept
chapters.summary: Grandmother Adunni arrives unannounced and reveals the Montrose covenant: for six generations, one family member has lived in Well House, feeding it silence, secrets, and small obediences so it would never hunger for the town. She begs Mirabel to sign the appraisal honestly and walk away. POV: Mirabel. Beat: love against duty begins—Adunni's protection is also a cage.

chapters.title: The Tenant Below
chapters.summary: Mirabel finds the cellar well, and at its bottom, something that speaks in the voices of everyone she has ever failed. It knows her childhood habit of hiding and offers her a bargain: invisibility forever, in exchange for Theo. She refuses and runs. POV: Mirabel. Beat: the house's corruption made intimate—it corrupts through love, not fear.

chapters.title: Sale of the Century
chapters.summary: The buyer arrives early: a development consortium whose lead surveyor is a hollow-eyed woman Mirabel recognizes from the photographs—the previous covenant-keeper, consumed when her generation broke faith. The sale will starve the house into hunger. Theo is taken by the extra door. POV: Mirabel. Beat: rising panic; the cost of the old lie comes due.

chapters.title: Sunset Clause
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Adunni prepare for the night, salting thresholds and counting doors aloud, while Adunni confesses she once fed the house Mirabel's grandfather. Mirabel's forgiveness is interrupted when the lights fail and every door in the house opens at once. POV: Mirabel, with Adunni's confession in dialogue. Beat: the found family fractures under truth, then holds.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Mirabel descends to the well to bargain for Theo, enduring a gauntlet of rooms that rearrange to keep her invisible, small, and obedient—the house weaponizing her whole life's training. She reaches the well at 3 a.m. and hears Theo answering her voice from below. POV: Mirabel. Beat: climax of will; invisibility refused at every step.

chapters.title: A Harvest for the Well
chapters.summary: At the well's mouth, Mirabel offers the house not Theo, not a stranger, but her own inheritance: every secret she was raised to keep, spoken aloud, including the truth of her parents' deaths. The covenant, built on silence, cannot digest truth; the house convulses, the extra door closes on the thing behind it, and Theo is returned—changed, but himself. POV: Mirabel. Beat: climax and sacrifice—love against duty resolved by truth against power.

chapters.title: Sunrise, Appraised
chapters.summary: Dawn finds Well House merely old: smaller inside, honest in its measurements, its photographs empty of extra chairs. Adunni, freed of the covenant, chooses at last to leave; Mirabel appraises the house at its true value and files the report. Theo stays on as caretaker of nothing in particular, and Mirabel, visible at last, lets herself be seen. POV: Mirabel. Beat: resolution—found family intact, the haunted inheritance ended.
